title: Babur Challenges Nanak's Authority and Marches to Meet Him

blocks.text: Babur reacts skeptically when Daulat Khan says Guru Nanak can bestow or withhold sovereignty. He asks who Nanak is to grant kingship and then resolves that let us go and see him, treating the encounter as a test of spiritual claim rather than an act of devotion.

His tone remains threatening as well as curious. Babur says that if the saint proves false he should be punished or converted, while if he is genuine Babur will judge the matter from direct experience rather than rumor.

The army therefore advances toward the Guru with a mixture of challenge and expectation. As the page closes, the narrative prepares the meeting by placing Babur's political ambition alongside the Guru's unhurried spiritual authority.
